title: RENALIS
text: RENALIS is a research prototype for a focused dialysis question. When blood pressure is declining, several physiological explanations may fit the same available record. Our aim is to make those explanations visible, show how their hypothetical responses differ, and ask which feasible additional observation could improve that comparison. This demonstration covers the working software, the data and equations behind it, the evaluations we actually ran, and the evidence we still need. The built-in patients, their preceding sessions and the acquisition streams are fictional. A separate retrospective benchmark uses the public HEMOBP dataset. These two evidence sources remain distinct throughout the product. The project does not identify a patient's actual diagnosis, establish causal treatment effects, or send treatment settings to a dialysis machine. Its contribution is an inspectable workflow for reasoning about uncertainty. We will follow that workflow through the interface, including cases where the model remains uncertain or should withhold a comparison.

title: The research question
text: During dialysis, fluid removal interacts with circulating volume, refill from tissue and physiological compensation. A pressure trace alone does not uniquely identify all of those hidden processes. In our authored model, different response families can fit a similar observed past while projecting different responses to a hypothetical removal profile. That creates a practical research question. Before favoring one comparison, what additional evidence would actually change the conclusion? RENALIS keeps the hypotheses separate and shows their assumptions. It also distinguishes a modeled future crossing from a current low pressure reading. A current event is already happening in the observed record, so it must not appear as an advance warning. The numeric threshold is a declared research endpoint rather than a complete clinical assessment. Symptoms and review context belong alongside the measurements. Throughout this demonstration, hypothetical profiles remain simulations. We have not established that changing a profile produces the modeled effect in real patients.

title: The evidence journey
text: The main entry point is the Evidence journey. It keeps one patient and one replay cutoff across six connected sections. Learn shows how preceding sessions influence the starting prior. Understand exposes the current model state and its equations. Compare retains the competing explanations. Ask previews possible measurement results and compares their modeled value. Review keeps the observations, failures, corrections and notes together. Verify shows the retrospective and independent synthetic evaluations. The recorded interface uses Meera, a fictional patient, at minute eighty. That starting point permits an uninterrupted research experiment. Moving the replay clock changes which observations are available. It does not grant the estimator access to later readings or future machine changes. The patient and minute also appear in the local URL so the state can be reopened. A page view does not automatically acquire a measurement, reset an experiment or rewrite an existing report. Those actions require explicit controls in the workspace.

title: The software architecture
text: The architecture separates the physiological sandbox from the observed-data benchmark. Raw preceding synthetic sessions enter a history learner. Available blood pressure and machine records pass through cutoff and quality gates. Their information initializes and updates four authored physiological families. The observation-policy calculation then evaluates possible measurements under explicit noise, timing, failure and burden assumptions. The frontend presents those calculations and records the review context in a local SQLite database. Acquisitions and corrections feed back through the same evidence gates. Saved reports retain their original evidence and revision. React and TypeScript implement the interface, while FastAPI and NumPy support the backend. The observed HEMOBP path audits public tables, constructs patient-separated evaluation sets and exports aggregate results. Its trained models do not silently replace the synthetic fluid model. That separation matters because a retrospective prediction result cannot validate every physiological equation or hypothetical intervention displayed elsewhere in the product.

title: Learning from preceding sessions
text: Earlier versions used an authored patient refill prior. The current release replaces that shortcut with a learner consuming raw preceding-session trajectories. Each fictional patient has six completed sessions containing blood pressure readings and machine settings. A grid likelihood fits refill and compensation conditional on the declared equations. The result shrinks toward a population reference and retains an uncertainty floor. The interface exposes the population value, the learned value, the number of sessions and a digest identifying the source history. Expanding the section reveals each session's fitted refill and pressure error. A separate forward-session ablation fits four preceding sessions and scores two later sessions. That checks whether the historical input reaches the prediction process. It does not prove clinical personalization. The synthetic generator and learner share model structure, and different hidden parameters can still explain similar observations. The current session and records unavailable before the cutoff do not enter historical learning.

title: The physiological graph
text: The model graph makes the internal quantities inspectable. Tissue fluid and circulating volume are estimated compartments. Available machine removal is an observed synthetic setting. The transition transfers refill from tissue to plasma and removes fluid through the machine, preserving mass within the declared accounting. Blood pressure constrains model compatibility through the pressure-response equations. Cardiac output is an authored sensor proxy rather than a measured value until an observation is acquired. Clicking a node reveals its equation and provenance. These distinctions prevent a polished body graphic from looking like a patient scan or a direct measurement of hidden physiology. Conservation tests verify a mathematical property of the implementation. They cannot establish that the pressure equation is correct for real patients. The graph is therefore a readable declaration of model structure. It gives reviewers a concrete place to challenge assumptions, trace inputs and identify which quantities require matched physiological measurements.

title: Competing explanations
text: RENALIS now keeps four response families: volume and refill limitation, vascular compensation limitation, cardiac response limitation, and a mixed response hypothesis. Each family retains forty-eight particles and sees the same available blood pressure and machine history. The cards show factual fit error, relative compatibility and the modeled pressure under the selected hypothetical profile. A similar factual fit can coexist with a different projected response. Selecting another family changes the explanation in focus without acquiring new evidence. Changing the hypothetical removal rate recomputes the comparison from the shared cutoff. Compatibility weights are conditional on this chosen model bank. They are not probabilities that the patient has a particular clinical diagnosis. Adding a mixed family expands the authored possibilities, but the patient's actual physiology may still be absent. When observations contradict every available explanation, the correct response is to downgrade authority. The product must preserve that unresolved state rather than force a confident winner.

title: Possible measurement results
text: Before acquiring an observation, the Ask section shows what each explanation expects. The channels are repeat cuff pressure, relative blood volume and cardiac output. Conditional predictive ranges include the declared sensor noise and update when the selected noise multiplier or observation timing changes. Overlap between ranges makes limited discrimination visible. The expanded preview shows lower, middle and higher possible results, their hypothetical support updates and the profile preferred under the declared loss. None of those previews becomes an acquired observation. They are computed possibilities. Equipment settings constrain what the unit can actually request. A basic configuration permits only cuff pressure, while other configurations enable relative volume or all research channels. Unavailable channels remain inspectable for comparison, but the server rejects their acquisition. The noise distributions and sensor equations are authored research assumptions. We have not calibrated these ranges against matched clinical device observations, so their visual precision must not be mistaken for clinical certainty.

title: Whole-policy observation value
text: A measurement can be informative without improving the decision being compared. RENALIS therefore displays information gain separately from expected decision-loss reduction. The whole-policy calculation starts with the best immediate profile under the declared research loss. It compares that baseline with waiting for an observation, possible acquisition failure and choosing a later profile after a result. Removal continues at the current setting while waiting. Failed acquisition supplies no new information but retains its burden. Gaussian quadrature integrates possible values, and negative expected value remains visible. A declared burden multiplier and delay penalty produce the net value. At default costs, no available measurement may clear the threshold. That is an allowed abstention, not a broken recommendation. Changing a cost assumption is a research sensitivity analysis. It does not establish a real device price or clinical utility. The numerical reference check also remains a diagnostic check rather than a global guarantee of integration accuracy.

title: The evidence lifecycle
text: The acquisition ledger records what was requested, when it becomes available, whether it succeeded and what burden it incurred. Valid observations update support only after release. Artifacts remain in the record but do not enter inference. A manual research observation has an observation time and an availability time, allowing delayed release without pretending the value was measured later. Repeated requests reuse the existing observation instead of counting it twice. Corrections append a new record with a reason and a link to the earlier value. Rewinding before the correction restores the earlier available evidence. Saved comparisons preserve their original settings, evidence identifiers and revision even after a later correction or archive. Review notes provide a place for symptoms, uncertainty and handover context. This local prototype does not implement a clinical identity or deployment system. The lifecycle demonstrates a reproducible evidence contract that can be tested before any real integration is considered.

title: The observed-data result
text: The retrospective HEMOBP evaluation asks a separate prediction question. Given a currently non-low pressure reading, it predicts the next distinct measured reading at a gap between five and thirty-five minutes. Fit, calibration and test patients are disjoint. The test set contains sixty-one thousand nine hundred forty-seven windows from one hundred seventy-six patients. Mean absolute error is twelve point one nine four millimeters of mercury for persistence, eleven point three five six for dynamic inputs, eleven point three two eight after demographics, and eleven point one six one with preceding-session history. The paired history increment is minus zero point one six six five millimeters of mercury. Its patient-cluster interval remains below zero under this protocol. That supports a small retrospective predictive contribution from history. It does not establish clinically meaningful improvement, physiological identification or prospective benefit. The displayed figures come from the saved evaluation output, with the cohort assumptions and exclusions retained.

title: Observed-data limitations
text: The audit found an approximately eight-hour difference between session clocks and machine-table timing. The pipeline declares that shift as an empirical alignment assumption and checks elapsed-time consistency. Source clock semantics still need independent confirmation. Under these rules, about two point five million of four point four million machine packets match usable intervals. Such substantial exclusions can bias the cohort. The event model's sensitivity is sixty-one point two five percent and its positive predictive value is thirteen point five one percent. Missed events and false alerts remain important limitations. A nominal ninety-percent empirical residual range covers eighty-six point seven four percent of test readings, so undercoverage remains visible too. The report includes calibration bins, recurrent-event context and a thirty-minute refractory alarm rule. These are retrospective workload summaries. They cannot establish how many interruptions a real dialysis unit would experience, and the next-measured-reading endpoint does not observe every continuous hypotensive episode.

title: The independent policy holdout
text: The independent synthetic study retains one hundred ninety-two cases across eight regimes. The scoring futures use additive response curves different from the twin's pressure equations. The regimes include mixed and omitted mechanisms, noisy sensors, basic equipment and delayed or failed acquisition. Four policies share the available values and an at-most-one-observation budget. Mean independent regret is about zero point two two two for fixed cuff and zero point two four one for decision value. Lower is better. Decision value therefore does not beat cuff overall. Its paired difference is positive, and the uncertainty interval includes zero. The interface also reports tails, acquisitions, cases worse than cuff and a descriptive confident-wrong count. Every policy record remains available. A documented oracle-grid correction includes permitted waiting-prefix profiles, while the initial report is preserved. No policy was changed after inspecting these results. Further development must use a separately declared evaluation instead of relabeling this frozen task as fresh evidence.

title: The model's stopping conditions
text: A complete demonstration includes the states where the model should withhold a comparison. Moving Meera to minute ninety-five produces a current low pressure observation. The interface calls it an existing event and removes experiment authority. Leela at minute ninety demonstrates stale pressure evidence, while a completed session has no future treatment horizon. An extreme manual relative-volume observation demonstrates contradiction with the authored bank. Those cases retain factual evidence and review context without manufacturing a reliable scenario ranking. Failed acquisitions and artifact observations remain visible in the audit. Equipment limits apply on the server as well as in the controls. A network error disables mutations and offers retry. The browser tests exercise these states, corrections, saved reports and five responsive widths. Passing software checks establishes selected implementation properties under the test fixtures. It does not establish clinical safety or validate an emergency response. No treatment command leaves this research workspace.

title: Longitudinal and interoperability extensions
text: The optional longitudinal experiment carries the evidence-weighted fluid compartments through authored intervals and future sessions. Reviewers choose intake, residual output and the interval length. The model reports compartment totals and a numerical mass-balance error. Input changes or new evidence invalidate the previous result. This extension provides conditional fluid accounting. It does not predict future blood pressure, identify renal function or prescribe a target. Its residual-output map is deliberately simplified and needs paired longitudinal validation. The export experiment produces a synthetic FHIR version four collection containing a Patient, a Device and a measured systolic-pressure Observation. Internal references and units are checked. The collection is an interoperability example, not proof of ABDM profile conformance, certification or authorized hospital integration. Both extensions expose their assumptions so they can be reviewed and replaced with validated components when suitable data and clinical partnerships become available.

title: The next evidence gates
text: The local release now connects historical learning, competing hypotheses, possible measurements, whole-policy value and an auditable review process. Its evidence includes a small retrospective history increment and a policy holdout that does not show overall superiority. The next work is to confirm the source timing semantics and independently reproduce the audited cohort. An expert task study should assess whether people understand the distinctions between measurements, model states and hypotheses. Matched physiological observations are needed to calibrate the sensor and response equations. An approved silent external study can then evaluate calibration, workload and disagreement before any prospective impact claim. The protocol and capture schema prepare those studies, but no recruitment, institutional approval or patient outcome has been invented. The architecture, presentation, model card and reproducible reports accompany the software. Actual team details, public repository access, an unlisted video upload and the organizer submission remain entrant-controlled steps. The project is ready for careful review as a research prototype.
